result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You need to come back for more tests. This follows your breast screening mammogram (breast x-ray) on 16 September 2026. This is called a recall.

Being called back does not mean you have cancer. About 4 in 5 women who are called back do not have breast cancer.

## What you need to do
1. Go to your appointment at the Breast Assessment Clinic, Eastmoor Hospital. It is on Wednesday 7 October 2026 at 11:00.
2. The visit may take up to 4 hours.
3. If you cannot come, call 01632 960 733 as soon as possible.

## Dates and medicines
- 16 September 2026: your breast screening mammogram.
- Wednesday 7 October 2026 at 11:00: your appointment at the Breast Assessment Clinic, Eastmoor Hospital.
- Medicines: the letter does not list any medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What tests will I have at the clinic?
- Can I bring someone with me?
- When will I get my results?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*

problems.explanation_says: Asks 'What tests will I have at the clinic?' and 'When will I get my results?' without giving answers.
problems.letter_says: You may have more mammograms, an ultrasound scan and, in some cases, a biopsy. You will usually get most of your results on the same day.
problems.why: The letter answers these questions, but the explanation leaves the answers out. The patient does not learn what to expect at the visit or when results usually come.

problems.explanation_says: Asks 'Can I bring someone with me?' as a question only.
problems.letter_says: You can bring a friend or family member with you.
problems.why: The letter gives this permission directly, but the explanation does not state it.

verifier.summary: The explanation is accurate. Dates, times, the phone number, the 4-in-5 statistic and the negation are all correct, and nothing is added. It only leaves out minor details: the possible tests, when results usually come, and that the patient can bring someone. The letter answers the questions the explanation suggests, but the explanation doesn't give those answers.
